I checked both files against the source, the frozen ground truth and score.mjs v1.1.0, and imported the scorer's own normalize/scoreCandidate read-only to test fixes. Scratch scripts are in <local scratch folder> five outputs are lossless:
- **CSV:** PackForAI document and MarkItDown parse back to exactly the source's 121x11 rows. The table body of PackForAI document is byte-identical to MarkItDown's, apart from the final newline. PackForAI compact is the source CSV itself, with only CRLF changed to LF and a 2-line header added. Python csv.reader returns rows equal to the source.
- **JSON:** MarkItDown's output is byte-identical to the source (same sha256). Both PackForAI outputs wrap the source unchanged in a ```json fence, byte-identical inside it.

The only scores below 1.0 in my files are PackForAI compact on gen-orders.csv: text_recall 0.85 and table recall, precision and F1 of 0. Both come from the scorer, not from lost content:
1. **Text recall:** the 3 missing phrases are in the output in standard RFC 4180 form (`""Fresh""`). The scorer accepts JSON's `\"` escapes only because normalization deletes backslashes. It has nothing that undoes CSV's doubled quotes. With the doubled-quote form also accepted, compact finds 20/20.
2. **Table recall:** only GFM pipe tables are parsed. When I turned the compact CSV into a pipe table and scored it with scoreCandidate, it got table recall 1.0.

Effect on the 9-file averages for compact: text_recall would go from 0.941 to about 0.958, and table_recall from 0.125 to 0.25 from this file alone. The csv-block parser change might also help the compact xlsx and pptx outputs, which I did not check.

No ground-truth issues:
- Every CSV must_contain item is one whole field. For example, 0.85 occurs 16 times, always as an exact field, and the ORD ids are unique.
- The JSON anchors are in document order, and the cursors do not contain record ids.

Tokens (o200k), source in brackets:
- **CSV [5795]:** document 6532, compact 5807, MarkItDown 6512. The document costs MarkItDown plus a 20-token preamble. Compact is 10.8% below MarkItDown but 12 tokens above the raw source. PackForAI's own sidecar reports savingsPercent -0.2.
- **JSON [3414]:** document 3442, compact 3433, MarkItDown 3414. Compact does no compacting: minified JSON would be 2273 tokens (-33%).

Neither tool has noise, absent or heading checks on these files (all null). The JSON file cannot tell the tools apart on content; only tokens differ.

pub-srpt-118-226.pdf: every score shared by the three candidates holds up. That is text_recall 0.692, heading_recall 0, table_recall 0, noise_excess 9 and absent_violations 4, and each one matches what the outputs really contain. I found no ground-truth errors. I checked the frozen GT against the rendered PDF pages (sha256 matches), including Table 1 at 200 dpi and the page-9 statute headings at 150 dpi. The headings, the table values (0 5 7 7 6 5 30), the 'WITH NON FEDERAL ENTITIES' wording and the four line-end splits (require-/ments, per-/sistent, effec-/tiveness, chal-/lenges) are all correct.

Two things should be said when these numbers are published.

(1) The 0.69 text recall is not lost content. All four missing must_contain phrases fail only because the tools keep line-end hyphens ('au- dits', 'find- ings', 'des- ignated', 'require- ments'). If 'letter- letter' is joined, every candidate finds 13/13. The same defect is counted a second time by absent_violations (4), so hyphenation costs about 0.31 text recall plus 4 absent violations, identically for both tools.

(2) The scores tie, but the outputs differ in quality, and the scorer does not see it. MarkItDown breaks justified body text on PDF pages 3-4 into 15 false pipe tables (43 lines). The scorer's rule that turns '|' into a space hides this, and no metric penalises extra tables. One of these tables splits the heading 'II. BACKGROUND AND NEED FOR THE LEGISLATION' across two rows. MarkItDown also joins footnote numbers to the citations that follow them, which produces wrong citations: '131 U.S.C.', '52 CFR', '931 U.S.C.'. It prints the invisible rotated slug backwards ('STROPER htiw DORP32NQ621KSD no eromligj') 10 times, once in the middle of footnote 7, and it garbles the table's last column header into '2 2 0 0 2 2 4 9 –'.

PackForAI has no false tables and no merged citations, and its table header can still be read ('2024–'/'2029'). But it runs a fallback mode that puts every page inside a ```text code fence, so the output has no Markdown structure. It also keeps the extra spaces from justified text: 2115 runs of 2 or more spaces cost about 2116 tokens, 27% of its output.

Tokens: packforai.document 7858 and compact 7854, against markitdown 6504, so PackForAI is about 21% larger despite having 5% fewer characters. With the space runs collapsed, PackForAI would be 5742 tokens, about 12% below MarkItDown. The 'compact' (token-optimised) output saves 4 tokens over 'document', and PackForAI's own run metadata reports savingsPercent -1.7.

MarkItDown spends 1150 tokens on its false-table lines; the same text without table syntax is 336 tokens. It also spends 297 tokens on the reversed slug text.

summary:
pub-fedreg-2024-31144.pdf: I opened all three outputs, rendered pages 1-4 at 110 dpi, and re-ran the scorer's own normalize() through a scratch script. No ground-truth errors: Tables 1 and 3, the headings, the line-end hyphens and the white (invisible) GPO slug all match the rendered pages.

MarkItDown's text recall of 0/14 is REAL. pdfminer joins lines that sit side by side in the 3 columns, so on every page each output line holds pieces of 2-3 columns. Its longest unbroken run per phrase is 5-10 words out of 9-26. Its order score of 0.375 is REAL, and if anything generous.

PackForAI's 13/14 is a SCORER_ARTIFACT. The one miss is the true compound '40,000-pound', which PackForAI writes as '40,000-' then a line break, then 'pound'. The scorer turns the line break into a space. A one-rule fix ('- ' becomes '-' on both sides) makes the phrase match, and all 3 absent checks still catch the split words in both outputs.

Heading recall is 0 for both, and that is REAL. PackForAI puts every page inside a ```text code fence, and MarkItDown emits no headings at all. The tie hides a real difference: all 12 heading texts stand alone on their own lines in PackForAI, but only 2/12 in MarkItDown.

Table recall is 0 for both, also REAL: neither tool writes Tables 1 or 3 as pipe tables. MarkItDown does write 16 junk pipe tables on page 4 (872 tokens) that mix three columns of text.

Noise is a REAL tie at excess 6 each. Both keep 3 running headers and the invisible 'Jkt 265001' slug on all 4 pages.

Absent checks: PackForAI's 3 violations are REAL. MarkItDown's 2 understates its problem. Its third split word ('Destina- tion') escapes detection only because its output is more garbled: 'Destina- applicable fees ... tion Markets'. Neither output contains 'Destination' anywhere. This SCORER_ARTIFACT favours MarkItDown and reverses the true order on this check.

Tokens: PackForAI document 6755 and compact 6751, against MarkItDown 6560 (+3.0%), REAL. PackForAI spends about 326 tokens on runs of spaces and 69 on code fences and page headers. Its compact output saves nothing here: 4 tokens, and the sidecar reports -1.4% savings. MarkItDown spends 872 tokens on junk tables. Both spend 179 tokens on dot leaders and about 320 on invisible slugs. Scratch scripts are in <local scratch folder> (check.mjs, headings.mjs, pg-1..4.png).

findings.evidence: "This section of the FEDERAL REGISTER Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and fee structure of the Specialty Crop" — every body line on pp.1-4 mixes 2-3 columns; longest contiguous run per must_contain phrase is only 5-10 of 9-26 words.
